permissions.label: Compile requirements
permissions.description: Author the work: turn a requirement into a plan and its task, and design a Blueprint.

permissions.label: Steer plans
permissions.description: Answer or defer a plan’s questions, re-compile it and dispatch it.

permissions.label: Move tasks
permissions.description: Change a task’s status and tick its checklist.

permissions.label: Run agents
permissions.description: Start an agent run in its own worktree, stop it, and discard its branch.

permissions.label: Use sessions
permissions.description: Ask in a session and let it read this project’s code with the tools.

permissions.label: Read other people’s sessions
permissions.description: Open a session someone else started, and its transcript, files and export. Your own are always yours.

permissions.label: Write workflows
permissions.description: Create, edit and archive workflows. Running one needs the plan permissions.

permissions.label: Approve gated actions
permissions.description: Sign or refuse migrations, deploys and other high-risk actions.

permissions.label: Merge a run
permissions.description: Merge an accepted run’s branch into the repository on this machine.

permissions.label: See this machine’s delivery
permissions.description: The DevOps screen: services, checks, deliveries, logs and containers on the machine the API runs on.

permissions.label: Give final verdicts
permissions.description: Accept a review or send it back, open or cancel the production gate, and mark a test as expected to fail.

permissions.label: Write tool rules
permissions.description: Allow, ask or deny what agents, sessions and tools may do — edits, commands, web access and MCP calls — for the workspace or one project.

permissions.label: Curate memory
permissions.description: Add, pin and archive facts, and settle conflicts between them.

permissions.label: Use AI features
permissions.description: Ask memory, brainstorm, and extract facts from text.

permissions.label: Write evals
permissions.description: Author eval suites and their cases, and override a result.

permissions.label: Onboard projects
permissions.description: Clone or read a repository and measure it.

permissions.label: Manage tools
permissions.description: Register MCP servers.

permissions.label: Manage custom agents
permissions.description: Write the workspace's and projects' own agents: their prompts, lanes and the tools they may ask for — never more than the tool rules allow.

permissions.label: Change screen settings
permissions.description: Switch skills, plugins, hooks, commands and models on or off.

permissions.label: Manage people
permissions.description: Create accounts, assign roles, reset passwords and disable access.

permissions.label: Manage roles
permissions.description: Create and edit custom roles.

permissions.label: Manage teams
permissions.description: Create teams and choose their members.

permissions.label: Read the audit log
permissions.description: See who signed in and who changed access, keys or settings.

permissions.label: See who is in the workspace
permissions.description: The directory: names, roles and teams. Changing any of them needs Manage people.

permissions.label: Administer the workspace
permissions.description: The workspace name, AI providers and keys, and resetting data.

permissions.label: Use this machine
permissions.description: Browse and open folders on the machine the API runs on, edit files there, open a terminal, and run or debug a project.

roles.name: Owner
roles.description: Everything, including access and keys. There is always at least one.

roles.name: Admin
roles.description: Runs the workspace: people, roles, keys and every screen.

roles.name: AI Project Manager
roles.description: Steers the work and signs the gates: the final approver.

roles.name: Engineer
roles.description: Works the board and curates memory. Cannot sign the gates.

agents.name: AI Commander
guardrails: Must produce a plan before any agent runs
HIGH risk always escalates to human
agents.systemPrompt: You are the AI Commander. You never write code. You compile requirements, decompose work, assign agents, gate risk and escalate to the human PM.

agents.name: Architect
guardrails: Must cite evidence files for every claim
Flags legacy contract breaks as HIGH
agents.systemPrompt: Map the blast radius before anything is changed. Prefer the existing pattern over a better one.

agents.name: Researcher
agents.systemPrompt: Search four ways before concluding. Every finding needs a citation and a confidence.

agents.name: Frontend Engineer
guardrails: Must run visual diff before handoff
agents.systemPrompt: Match the surrounding code exactly. Never introduce a new state library. Screenshot-verify every UI change.

agents.name: Backend Engineer
agents.systemPrompt: Strict SOLID. Class-object naming per project rules. Never bypass the repository layer.

agents.name: Database Engineer
agents.systemPrompt: TRANS_* tables are append-only. Every migration ships with a verified rollback.

agents.name: DevOps Engineer
agents.systemPrompt: Every deploy needs a rollback path proven before it ships.

agents.name: QA Engineer
agents.systemPrompt: Never claim a test passes. Run it. Attach the output.

agents.name: Security Engineer
agents.systemPrompt: Assume the input is hostile. Report the class of issue, never a working exploit.

agents.name: Code Reviewer
guardrails: Cannot approve its own agents work twice
Must cite file:line for every finding
agents.systemPrompt: You are the last gate before the human. Refuse anything that breaks a legacy contract, even if it is technically better.

agents.name: Documentation Agent
guardrails: Must link to a commit or memory fact
agents.systemPrompt: Document the why, never the what. Link every decision to its evidence.

agents.name: Vision Agent
guardrails: Must identify the source component before editing
agents.systemPrompt: Given a screenshot, find the exact component in the repository before proposing anything.
